title: Multi-source in-transit visibility fusion for contested movement (RFID, satellite trackers, carrier EDI and manifests into a trusted COP that survives disconnected legs)
problem: USTRANSCOM and its components still cannot produce a near-real-time, end-to-end, trusted picture of where DoD cargo is because tracking evidence arrives from heterogeneous sources (active/passive RFID reads, Iridium/mesh trackers, carrier EDI status messages, service manifests) with latency and coverage gaps that widen on contested or disconnected legs, so the May 2026 USTRANSCOM CSO explicitly asks industry for a prototype that ingests, fuses and visualizes those sources into a trusted COP.
echelons: Theater (TSC/ESC distribution management centers, theater distribution centers, aerial/sea ports of debarkation)

user.exact_role: Movement/ITV analysts and watch officers in the USTRANSCOM Deployment and Distribution Operations Center (DDOC) and Fusion Center; 618th Air Operations Center (Tanker Airlift Control Center) airlift/aerial-port controllers; distribution integration branch staff in theater sustainment commands; port/aerial-port cargo operations NCOs who physically read tags
organization_examples: Military Surface Deployment and Distribution Command (SDDC) port operations
DLA Distribution / DLA Troop Support (Turbo Fusion 2026 partner)
Theater Sustainment Commands (e.g., 8th TSC, 21st TSC) distribution management centers
Army Contested Logistics CFT (requirements sponsor, not buyer)

current_workflow: Cargo is built, tagged (active RFID on containers/large items, passive RFID/barcode on pallets and pieces) and manifested in service deployment systems (TC-AIMS II, GATES, CMOS, IBS) at origin.

Tag reads and manifest events are captured at fixed RFID interrogators/portals at installations, ports and nodes; commercial carriers send EDI status messages (e.g., 214/315-class) for CONUS and commercial legs.

Feeds flow into IGC (IDE/GTN Convergence), the DoD system of record for ITV/asset visibility, which correlates them into shipment/asset records; analysts query IGC and carrier portals and receive automated alerts where configured.
Aggregated, delayed data is analysed in USTRANSCOM's Pegasus environment on Advana for decision support; watch officers assemble slides and status reports for the DDOC and CCMD J4s.

For high-priority or unaccounted cargo, staff chase status by phone/e-mail with carriers, port operators and units; on austere/contested legs with no interrogators or connectivity the record simply goes dark until the next read.

In exercises (Valiant Shield 24, Turbo Fusion 25/26) supplemental mesh/satellite tags (LMI NADACS/SPECTR) were added to selected cargo so that dashboards could show near-real-time position; this is trial, not enterprise, practice.
current_solution: IGC (IDE/GTN Convergence) as ITV system of record, sustained since Feb 2025 under a ~$27M USTRANSCOM task order to D&G Support Services (WOSB set-aside); RFID-IV/aRFID-V hardware (Savi active tags, readers, Iridium SATCOM kits, portable deployment kits); carrier EDI feeds validated only loosely (DoDIG 2014 found USTRANSCOM did not test contractor EDI used to verify performance); Pegasus/Advana analytics (CDAO); GDSS for airlift; exercise-only mesh/Iridium tagging via LMI NADACS/SPECTR (Valiant Shield 2024, Turbo Fusion late 2025 and 2026). Workarounds: manual tag reads, phone/e-mail chasing, spreadsheets and slide-built COPs.
failure: Fusion and trust, not tagging, is the failure point: (1) each source reports on its own cadence and identifier scheme (TCN, container ID, tag ID, carrier PRO/BOL), so IGC records show stale or conflicting last-known positions rather than a confidence-scored estimate; (2) coverage depends on fixed interrogator infrastructure and carrier EDI, both absent on contested, austere or allied-port legs, so the picture goes dark exactly when it matters; (3) validation of carrier-submitted EDI is weak, so a 'trusted' COP is not established; (4) exercise-proven mesh/satellite tags feed separate dashboards rather than the system of record, adding another silo; (5) the enterprise picture is not consumable at the tactical edge when disconnected.

evidence.claim: USTRANSCOM CSO HTC71126SCSO1 Specific AoI 001 'In-Transit Visibility Modernization for Global Defense Logistics' seeks a scalable, interoperable, secure prototype delivering near-real-time, end-to-end ITV of DoW cargo and assets that creates a trusted COP by ingesting, fusing and visualizing data from a variety of tracking sources; posted 2026-05-20, Phase 1 solution briefs due 2026-06-04 via Vulcan. A solicitation phrased this way is direct government acknowledgement that the fused, trusted COP does not exist today.
evidence.source_title: TRANSCOM CSO - Specific AoI 001: In-Transit Visibility Modernization for Global Defense Logistics (aggregator mirror of sam.gov notice)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The USTRANSCOM base CSO is a standing vehicle (reported open until Feb 1, 2036) with specific AoIs issued against it; ITV modernization is the first specific AoI, and USTRANSCOM has been publicly soliciting industry for contested-logistics solutions since at least 2023 (DVIDS). Award status of AoI 001 as of Sept 2026: Public evidence insufficient.
evidence.source_title: USTRANSCOM Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) - Open Until February 1, 2036 (BW&CO summary); DVIDS: USTRANSCOM seeks industry solutions for contested logistics
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO has flagged ITV/asset-visibility shortfalls repeatedly for two decades: GAO-06-366R (2006) found lack of visibility over shipments heightens loss/theft risk and readiness impact and criticised active-RFID tag reuse; GAO-13-201 (Feb 2013) reviewed unresolved ITV issues including enforcement of RFID requirements on OCONUS cargo; GAO-16-88 (Dec 2015) reviewed the FY2014 NDAA-mandated DoD asset-tracking/ITV strategy; GAO-17-183 (2017) found improved performance measures and information still needed. Persistence across 2006-2017 shows an institutional, not merely technical, problem.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoDIG-2014-058 found USTRANSCOM contracting officials did not test contractor-submitted EDI transactions used to verify contractor performance because they had not developed internal-control procedures to validate ITV data - i.e., carrier EDI feeding the ITV picture was not validated, undermining 'trust' in the COP.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO-21-125 (2021) found DoD could better leverage contested-mobility capabilities, situating ITV within the broader contested-logistics readiness problem.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: In Exercise Valiant Shield 2024, Air Mobility Command trialed LMI's NADACS/SPECTR mesh-tag ITV solution and found it 'far more accurate than current manual reading methods'; in Operation Turbo Fusion (late 2025) 400+ pieces of cargo were tagged with SPECTR mesh tags to get near-real-time monitoring from CONUS staging yards to overseas mission locations, with ITV a 'key tenet' of the exercise. Both are exercise trials layered on top of the enterprise system, i.e., documented workarounds for the enterprise ITV shortfall; vendor/trade-association accounts, not government evaluation reports.
evidence.source_title: NDTA: NADACS and Mesh Technology Boosts Logistics Decisional Advantage in USTRANSCOM's Turbo Fusion Exercise; ExecutiveBiz: Air Mobility Command Demonstrates LMI's SPECTR Platform
evidence.pub_date: 2025-2026 (NDTA; exact date not retrievable - egress blocked); 2024 (ExecutiveBiz)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The ITV stack is fragmented across at least five partial solutions: IGC as system of record (sustainment task order ~$27M to D&G Support Services, awarded 2025-02-28 over 13 other bidders, scope includes software development, cloud migration and RMF support); Savi RFID-IV ($102M, 2014-2020) and aRFID-V ($45M ceiling) hardware including Iridium SATCOM kits; LMI NADACS/SPECTR mesh/Iridium tags (platform launched Dec 2025 after IP acquisition); Pegasus on Advana (CDAO) for analytics; and DIU's Joint Sustainment Decision Tool prototypes (Air Space Intelligence, Watchtower Labs Jan 2026; Gallatin AI Jul 2026) for distribution planning. None is positioned as the source-agnostic fusion layer.
evidence.source_title: OrangeSlices: D&G Solutions awarded USTRANSCOM IGC contract; Savi RFID-IV press; WashingtonExec: LMI launches SPECTR (Dec 2025); DIU JSDT award notice
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Logistics decision-support is the fastest-cadence DIU lane in 2025-26: JSDT launched Aug 2025, prototype OTs to Air Space Intelligence and Watchtower Labs in Jan 2026, Gallatin AI added for USAREUR-AF in Jul 2026. These are prototypes, not deployments, and target distribution planning rather than ITV fusion, but they show new entrants can win adjacent joint-logistics work.
evidence.source_title: DIU: Two contracts awarded to modernize decision making for DoW's joint logistics enterprise
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: No discrete budget line for contested-logistics C2 or ITV fusion software was identified in the study's FY2026 budget sweep; IGC is understood to be funded through USTRANSCOM's Transportation Working Capital Fund and O&M sustainment rather than an RDT&E program element (RECALL - not re-verified this session; the planned budget-justification search could not be executed because the session search quota was exhausted).
evidence.label: HYPOTHESIS

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: There is one buyer (USTRANSCOM, with DLA as co-owner of IGC) and the interface to that buyer's data is controlled by an incumbent-sustained system of record (IGC, sustained by D&G under a WOSB set-aside, with Leidos/Peraton-class primes historically involved - RECALL). The tag/reader installed base (Savi RFID-IV/aRFID-V, Iridium kits) and its data formats are fixed by contract, and real ITV feeds are CUI on NIPR/IL4-IL5, so a startup cannot even see representative data without a sponsor. The one firm with exercise-validated multi-source hardware-plus-software (LMI, a large government consultancy, NADACS/SPECTR) is not a startup and already has Valiant Shield 24 and Turbo Fusion 25/26 trials, giving it the inside track on the May 2026 CSO. Commercial visibility platforms (project44/FourKites-class - RECALL, not verified this session) have the fusion technology for carrier EDI/telematics but lack DoD accreditation and the RFID/military-manifest side. Startups that did enter logistics (Watchtower, Air Space Intelligence, Gallatin) chose the less infrastructure-bound planning/optimization layer via DIU rather than the ITV fusion layer.
technical_wedge: A source-agnostic ITV fusion and entity-resolution engine that treats cargo like ISR tracks: (a) probabilistic association of heterogeneous observations (RFID reads, mesh/Iridium tracker pings, carrier EDI events, manifest/TCN records, AIS/ADS-B of the carrying platform) into a single shipment track with a confidence-scored, time-decayed location estimate rather than a 'last read'; (b) a dead-reckoning/route-model layer that keeps a plausible estimate alive across disconnected legs and flags divergence when a read finally arrives; (c) store-and-forward edge nodes (laptop/tablet at a port or aerial port) that keep a local COP and reconcile on reconnection; (d) EDI/observation trust scoring that addresses the validation gap DoDIG flagged. Built as a service that publishes back into IGC and Pegasus/Advana and outward to TAK/COP consumers, rather than as another dashboard.

mvp.what: An unclassified fusion engine plus thin COP that ingests simulated RFID/mesh reads, synthetic EDI 214/315-style status messages, synthetic TCN manifests and open AIS/ADS-B for the carrying vessel/aircraft, and emits confidence-scored shipment tracks that degrade gracefully when feeds drop; includes an offline edge node that reconciles with the enterprise node after a simulated 24-72 hour disconnect.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the software: a Turbo Fusion-like scenario (CONUS fort to port to overseas node) replayed with injected feed outages, showing track continuity, confidence bands, conflict detection between sources, and edge/enterprise reconciliation; measured against a naive 'last-read' baseline on synthetic ground truth.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That fusion measurably beats last-read (location error and time-to-detect divergence) under realistic outage patterns; that it can consume IGC/EDI-shaped data without bespoke code per source; that it runs disconnected; and, critically, that a sponsor (USTRANSCOM J3/J6, AMC A4, SDDC) will give access to real CUI feeds for a pilot - without that the MVP proves only algorithms.

data_requirement.what: Observation streams (active/passive RFID reads with reader IDs and timestamps; mesh/Iridium tracker pings; carrier EDI status events; TCN/manifest records from TC-AIMS II/GATES/IBS; GDSS mission data; AIS/ADS-B of carrying platforms) plus node/route reference data and ground truth for evaluation.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Open: AIS, ADS-B, EDI transaction-set formats (X12 214/315 specs are licensable), commercial carrier sandbox APIs, published RFID data models. Not obtainable without a sponsor: IGC/GDSS extracts, real manifests and tag reads (CUI, NIPR/IL4-IL5); exercise data from Turbo Fusion is held by USTRANSCOM/LMI. Realistic path: build on synthetic data, then a CRADA or CSO/OT pilot for CUI feeds; foreign-national access to CUI transportation data may need a technology control plan (counsel).

entry_vehicle.primary: USTRANSCOM CSO (HTC71126SCSO1) - next specific AoI or an unsolicited solution brief against the open base CSO; AoI 001's window closed 2026-06-04
sequence: Build unclassified synthetic-data MVP; seek CRADA or exercise participation (Turbo Fusion 2027, AMC experiments) to get CUI feed access
Respond to the next USTRANSCOM CSO AoI or DIU JSDT-adjacent CSO with a prototype OT (12-18 months, typically low single-digit $M if awarded)
In parallel, approach the AoI 001 awardee (if one is announced) or LMI/D&G as a fusion-engine subcontractor to get inside the IGC interface
Prototype OT with follow-on production OT or insertion into the IGC sustainment scope; ATO inheritance via Advana or the IGC boundary
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% U.S.-person ownership and U.S. principal place of business; the DoD SBIR preface requires disclosure of foreign nationals and export-control compliance, so an Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder with a large equity stake complicates SBIR (counsel needed; not a legal conclusion). CSO/OT and CRADA paths have no SBIR ownership test but FOCI review, CUI handling and any ITAR-controlled technical data still apply. ITV data itself is largely CUI rather than classified, which is more favorable than kinetic C2, but access for a non-U.S. person will need a technology control plan reviewed by counsel.

competition.how_close: Closest: end-to-end asset tracking and ITV platform combining long-life GPS, passive RFID, mesh tags over Iridium and dashboards; validated by AMC at Valiant Shield 2024 and used on 400+ cargo pieces in Turbo Fusion (late 2025); platform launched Dec 2025 after IP acquisition. Large government consultancy with USTRANSCOM relationships; likely CSO respondent.
competition.evidence: https://washingtonexec.com/2025/12/lmi-expands-sensor-mesh-capabilities-with-new-ip-acquisition-launch-of-spectr-platform/ (2025-12); https://www.executivebiz.com/articles/amc-lmi-spectr-valiant-shield-exercise (2024). Exercise accounts are vendor/trade-association sourced, not government evaluations.

competition.how_close: Owns the software-development and cloud-migration scope of the ITV system of record under a ~$27M task order (awarded 2025-02-28); any fusion capability the government wants inside IGC can be tasked here first.
Controls the active-RFID tag/reader/Iridium hardware and associated tracking software installed base ($102M RFID-IV 2014-2020; aRFID-V $45M ceiling).
Owns the analytics layer USTRANSCOM already uses on aggregated ITV data; could add fusion analytics as an Advana workload.
Army Vantage/Enterprise Agreement gives a DoD-wide data-integration vehicle; Palantir has done logistics/ITV-style fusion elsewhere but no USTRANSCOM ITV award verified.

competition.company: Air Space Intelligence, Watchtower Labs, Gallatin AI (DIU JSDT)
competition.how_close: Adjacent: distribution planning/decision tools under DIU prototype OTs (Jan and Jul 2026); they consume ITV rather than produce it, but could extend downward.
Have carrier-EDI/telematics fusion at scale commercially; no verified DoD ITV contract (RECALL - not re-verified this session; planned search not executed).
Supply-chain/acquisition analytics, not movement ITV; peripheral.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes. Palantir could stand up ITV fusion on Foundry under the Army EA or via Advana; LMI already has the hardware-plus-dashboard stack and exercise history; the IGC sustainer can be tasked to add fusion features; Anduril/L3Harris are less likely (not in logistics C2) but Anduril's Lattice fusion could be pointed at cargo if a customer asked.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it (1) delivers a demonstrably better fusion/entity-resolution core than the dashboard-oriented incumbents and (2) inserts as a service behind the existing IGC/Pegasus interfaces rather than competing for the front end, and (3) gets in through the CSO/OT door before an incumbent team is awarded. Given that AoI 001 responses closed June 2026 and an award (if any) would likely go to a team already exercised with USTRANSCOM, the honest reading is that the founders would be entering after the window, as a subcontractor at best. Reject as a standalone company thesis; keep as an option for a fusion-engine product that can also serve adjacent DDIL fusion problems.

capital_required.proof_of_concept_usd: 150k-300k (2 founders + 1 contractor, 6 months, synthetic-data fusion engine and edge node)
capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: 1.0M-2.5M (12-18 months: CRADA/exercise participation, CUI handling environment, IL4 hosting, 1-2 cleared/ex-USTRANSCOM logisticians, integration to IGC-shaped feeds); realistic only if funded by a CSO/OT prototype award
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: 5M-12M (RMF ATO in IGC or Advana boundary, 24x7 support, integration with GDSS/TC-AIMS II/carrier EDI, training of DDOC/618th AOC users)
capital_required.assumptions: Software-only; no tag hardware; ATO inherited from an existing boundary; single customer; award sizes for USTRANSCOM CSO prototypes are undisclosed, so the middle tier depends on winning one. Founder capital ($250k) covers only the proof of concept.

expertise_required.role: Former USTRANSCOM/AMC/SDDC movement-control or ITV subject-matter expert (DDOC, 618th AOC or port operations)
expertise_required.why: Knows IGC data semantics, TCN/RFID/EDI identifier chaos, exercise cadence and who sponsors CSO AoIs; without them the founders cannot get data or a champion.

expertise_required.role: Multi-source fusion / track-management engineer (ISR track fusion, probabilistic data association, entity resolution)
expertise_required.why: The technical wedge is fusion quality; dashboards are commoditized.
Carrier EDI (X12 214/315), DLMS and manifest formats are the bulk of the plumbing.
Any real pilot needs an IL4/IL5 environment and CUI controls; foreign-national access needs a technology control plan.
Non-U.S.-person co-founder, CUI transportation data, potential ITAR-controlled shipment details.

regulatory_burden.explanation: ITV data is predominantly CUI (not classified), but pilots require NIPR/IL4-IL5 hosting, RMF ATO (or inheritance), CUI handling and possibly DoD IT contractor access requirements; carrier data is commercially sensitive; movement of certain military cargo may involve ITAR-controlled technical data or OPSEC-sensitive unit movements. Not a legal judgment; counsel needed.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder is not an automatic bar to a CSO/OT or CRADA path, but: SBIR ownership/foreign-national rules would need review; CUI transportation data access is normally limited to authorized personnel and a technology control plan may be required; any ITAR-controlled technical data in manifests would be restricted; FOCI mitigation could be triggered if facility clearance is ever needed. Role split (business/product vs. engineering on CUI systems) should be designed with counsel before proposing.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Multimodal shipment fusion with confidence scoring and disconnected-edge operation is directly reusable for humanitarian logistics, mining/energy remote supply chains and allied militaries, but the commercial visibility market is already served by project44/FourKites-class platforms with far larger data networks; the differentiated part (DDIL tolerance, RFID/mesh fusion, trust scoring of carrier data) is a niche within that market.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility would come from being inside the IGC/Advana boundary with an ATO, having built the adapters for IGC/GDSS/EDI/RFID formats, and from exercise-validated fusion performance; the algorithms alone are reproducible by Palantir/LMI. Single-customer relationships are strong but non-transferable.

why_now: Three changes since 2023: (1) USTRANSCOM converted years of GAO/DoDIG findings into a specific commercial solicitation (CSO AoI 001, May 2026) with 'ingest, fuse, visualize' language; (2) cheap mesh/Iridium trackers proved in AMC's Valiant Shield 2024 and Turbo Fusion 2025/2026 that non-infrastructure tagging works, which multiplies the number of heterogeneous feeds needing fusion; (3) DIU's JSDT (2025-26) created a joint-logistics decision-tool lane that now needs better ITV inputs, and the Army/DoW contested-logistics push (CL-CFT, Indo-Pacific GAO work) keeps the problem funded politically. Against this, the 2026 ITV window may already have been taken by an incumbent team.
killer_risk: This is a single-buyer problem whose data interface (IGC) and hardware installed base are controlled by incumbents, and the only 2026 procurement window (CSO AoI 001) closed on 2026-06-04 - the likely awardee is a team that already exercised with USTRANSCOM (LMI-class), after which the government will have a prototype and no reason to fund a second. Two students without a USTRANSCOM insider cannot obtain CUI feeds, so the company would be building fusion algorithms on synthetic data for a customer that does not need a second vendor. Twenty years of GAO/DoDIG findings also show that ITV shortfalls are largely institutional (tagging compliance, EDI validation, process discipline) rather than an unsolved algorithm problem, which limits what software alone can fix.

allied_extension: Modestly more compelling with allies: NATO/Indo-Pacific coalition movements (e.g., through allied ports where U.S. RFID interrogators do not exist) are exactly the disconnected legs where fusion matters, and allied logisticians face the same problem with even less tagging infrastructure; a German co-founder gives access to Bundeswehr/BWI/Cyber Innovation Hub pilots and NATO logistics (JSEC/JLSG) forums. But allied ITV data sharing with a U.S. system of record is a policy problem (releasability, coalition networks) that a startup cannot solve, and EDF eligibility is lost if the company is U.S.-incorporated. Allied extension improves the story, not the near-term revenue.
